steps.instruction: Cook the rice according to package directions, using a little less water to avoid mushy, sticky rice. Let it cool uncovered; when it stops steaming, fluff with a fork and break it apart. Remaining clumps can be handled in the wok.
If refrigerating the rice overnight, break the cold clumps into individual grains by hand; rinse hands periodically with cold water if they become sticky.

Heat the wok over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon of the oil, then the beaten eggs; fold and scramble gently without scorching. Transfer the eggs back to their bowl. Separately, blanch the shrimp in boiling water, drain, and set aside.

Heat the wok now over high heat. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil and the diced onion. Stir-fry until the onions are translucent. Next, add the diced ham and Chinese roast pork, and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and stir-fry for 2 minutes, being sure to heat the rice uniformly. Use your wok spatula to flatten out and break up any remaining rice clumps.
Add the shrimp and peas, and stir-fry continuously for another 2 minutes until the rice is heated through.
Sprinkle salt and sugar over the rice. If using Shaoxing wine, drizzle it around the perimeter of the wok so it sizzles and the alcohol cooks off. Mix until seasonings are uniformly incorporated.

If the rice looks dry, sprinkle in some water or chicken stock, or add just a touch more oil. Adding liquid directly to large rice clumps helps break them up; too much water makes the rice soggy and too much oil makes it greasy.
Mix in the scrambled eggs, scallions, chopped lettuce, and white pepper. Stir-fry only until the lettuce is just wilted, then plate.

Do not overcook the lettuce; it should be just wilted to retain its refreshing crunch.
For dry rice, add only a little water, chicken stock, or oil: too much liquid makes it soggy and too much oil makes it greasy.
Serve with some hot sauce or chili oil on the side, if desired.

- 3 tablespoons oil
- 2 large eggs (beaten)

- 1/2 cup Chinese Roast Pork (about 4 ounces/110g)
- 3/4 cup frozen peas (thawed)
- 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
- ¼ teaspoon sugar
- 1 teaspoon Shaoxing wine (optional)
- 2 scallions (finely chopped)
- 2 cups romaine or iceberg lettuce (finely chopped)
- 1/8 teaspoon freshly ground white pepper
- use a little bit less water when cooking the rice; exact quantity not specified

- sprinkle in some water or chicken stock if the rice looks a little dry; exact quantity not specified
- a touch more oil if the rice looks a little dry; exact quantity not specified
- Serve your Young Chow Fried Rice with some hot sauce or chili oil on the side!
